title: Hypersurface presentation of a nonzero polynomial fibre
statement: Let A be a domain of characteristic zero, S an A[X]-algebra, and r a nonzero prime of A[X] contracting to zero in A. Let M be the image in S of the nonzero elements of A, and R = Localization M. There exists f in A[X] such that the residue-field fibre r.Fiber S is ring-isomorphic to R/(image f), and the image of the polynomial derivative f′ is a unit in that quotient. The polynomial ring and localization use [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 07PV, paragraph 4, and proof of Lemma 07PU, second paragraph

proof.text: Take K to be the residue field of the zero ideal of A, which Mathlib proves is a fraction field. Use Ideal.exists_mem_span_singleton_map_residueField_eq to choose f in r generating rK[X]. The hypothesis on contraction makes r disjoint from the nonzero constants, so localization preserves primality; injectivity preserves nonzeroness. Ideal.span_singleton_prime then shows the mapped f is irreducible. This is the fully proved private helper exists_irreducible_fibre_generator.

Construct the ring equivalence rather than choosing it from an unproved existence theorem. Evaluate K[X] in the explicit quotient Q=R/(image f), using the localization lift for coefficients. The generator identity kills r. Since K[X]/rK[X] is a field and localization contracts the extended prime back to r, every polynomial outside r maps to a unit of Q. Lift to the residue field and then to r.Fiber S by the tensor product universal property. In the other direction, nonzero base constants are units in r.Fiber S and f vanishes there, so localization followed by quotient gives a map Q to r.Fiber S. Tensor-product and residue-field extensionality prove one inverse law; quotient and localization extensionality prove the other. This is the fully proved private helper fibre_equiv_of_fraction_generator, which uses no characteristic-zero hypothesis.

Injectivity of A into K transfers characteristic zero. Irreducible.separable supplies the Bezout identity for the mapped f and its derivative. Evaluate that identity in Q, commute coefficient mapping with derivative, and use the vanishing of f to conclude that its derivative image is a unit. This is the fully proved private helper isUnit_derivative_of_separable_fraction. Combine the generator, equivalence and unit proofs to obtain the unchanged statement.

proof_origin.place: Proof of Lemma 07PU, second paragraph; characteristic-zero case of Proposition 07PV
proof_origin.note: R3, 2026-10-13: full Lean proof of the existing agent adaptation, using only proved Mathlib lemmas. All three private helpers compile without sorry. lean.statement:
theorem nonzero_fibre_hypersurface_presentation
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [CharZero A]
    (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra (Polynomial A) S]
    (r : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [r.IsPrime] (hr : r ≠ ⊥)
    (hrA : r.comap (C : A →+* Polynomial A) = ⊥) :
    let M := Submonoid.map
      ((algebraMap (Polynomial A) S).comp C).toMonoidHom (nonZeroDivisors A)
    let R := Localization M
    ∃ f : Polynomial A,
      Nonempty (r.Fiber S ≃+* R ⧸ Ideal.span ({algebraMap (Polynomial A) R f} : Set R)) ∧
      IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({algebraMap (Polynomial A) R f} : Set R))
        (algebraMap (Polynomial A) R (derivative f)))
